entry.content:
Fix NINJAL ZIP filename decoding on Python 3.14

Python 3.14's zipfile module already decodes non-UTF8-flagged
filenames correctly, so the cp437→cp932 roundtrip raises
UnicodeEncodeError. Fall back to the as-is filename when the
roundtrip fails.

entry.title: Make the whole dictionary the default build, and render each source's…
entry.content:
Make the whole dictionary the default build, and render each source's own markup (#2)

## One dictionary, not two

The repo built two artifacts from one codebase: a "public" release filtered down
to the two CC BY 4.0 sources, and a full local build of all ten. Everything
downstream of that split is gone — `publish_filter.py`, `audit_public_archive.py`,
`LICENSING.md`, the `_probe_ugd15_claims.py` audit, the five `-public` directory
trees, the `publish-filter`/`public`/`audit-public` targets, and the
`licenseTier` / `redistributable` / `permissionBasis` provenance keys that existed
only to feed the filter (also stripped from the committed source locks and the
acquisition scripts that wrote them).

`make` with no target now builds the whole dictionary: `.DEFAULT_GOAL := all`,
with `personal` as an alias that says what it is. 4,901 entries from all ten
sources, byte-reproducible, all gates green.

Per-source *attribution* stays — it is the product's core feature, not licensing
apparatus. Every card still names the source that made each statement, and
`tag_bank_1.json` and `index.json` still credit all ten. The repo's own MIT
LICENSE also stays: it governs this code, and deleting it would leave the
pipeline unlicensed.

## Each source's markup is part of its content

New `src/bugd/dialects.py`: the one place that knows which notation a source
writes. Measured over all 7,896 extracted points, the ten sources are two
dialects.

Yokubi writes GitHub-flavoured Markdown, and none of it rendered. Cards showed
literal `**asterisks**` (180 runs), a bare `|---------------|` separator as body
prose, 44 conjugation tables as run-together text, 48 bullets as dashes, and 149
backslash escapes verbatim. Worse, an escaped `\<verb\>` placeholder reached the
HTML parser as a tag opening and silently swallowed the rest of that paragraph.
It now renders as real `table`/`thead`/`ul`/`li` nodes and `span` emphasis, via
the HTML subset `richtext` already maps onto Yomitan's allowed tags — no new
schema surface. Blank header rows (33 of 44 tables) are dropped rather than drawn
as an empty band, and a contiguous pipe run is split at every separator row so
`lesson-20:の`'s four back-to-back tables stay four tables.

The other nine sources deliberately get no dialect. NINJAL's `<s>ます</s>` and
どんなとき's `<ruby>` already render correctly; `【…】` headings, `①②③` list breaks
and stripped-highlight soft breaks are already handled downstream. IMABI's 17,549
`N. ` lines and 145 `*` footnote markers are explicitly NOT read as Markdown —
its own prose cross-references those numbers as `Ex. N`, so an ordered list would
renumber them.

Two rendering fixes fall out of this:

* Yokubi ships zero blank lines and hard-wraps every paragraph, so the shared
  soft-wrap rule was gluing its English paragraphs into one run-on block.
* `proseTranslation` subordinates a Latin line inside a Japanese field. It was
  applied unconditionally, so for the five sources that explain IN English it
  indented and quietened the primary explanation. Now gated on the field's own
  language; the Japanese-field case is unchanged and still tested.

## Published index

`index.json` now carries `indexUrl`, `downloadUrl` and `isUpdatable`, and
`publish_dist` writes it beside the archive in `dist/` (committed, ~1KB) so a
reader can check the current revision without downloading 6MB. This is also a
hard requirement for installing the dictionary from a release: Hachidori refuses
any archive whose `indexUrl` does not match the URL it was fetched under.

## Verification

* `make test` — 719 passed (was 712; -21 for the deleted filter suite, +26 new
  dialect tests, +2 index tests).
* `make all` — 4,901 entries, 6,213,551 bytes, sha256 089f496d…; a clean rebuild
  reproduces the identical digest.
* `make validate` + `make validate-node` — both pass against the pinned 26.8.24.0
  schemas.
* `make audit-packaged`, `make audit-attribution`, `docs/contract/validate.py`,
  `check_example_runons.py` — no failures; 0 real run-ons; 0 colliding claims.
* Packaged bytes carry 44 tables, 38 `th`, 180 bold and 28 italic spans — exactly
  the measured Yokubi corpus counts. The 19 residual `**` are imabi/bunpro
  literal footnote markers, which must stay literal.

Co-authored-by: hermes <hermes@local>

entry.title: UGD-17: publish from the convergence lineage, with the fail-closed li…
entry.content:
UGD-17: publish from the convergence lineage, with the fail-closed licence filter

Reconciles `main` onto `ugd-16/converge`, whose tree this merge takes wholesale.
Two lineages both called themselves UGD-16 convergence; `main` had been published
from the wrong one.

WHY THIS TREE

`ugd-16/integration` (main's basis) is NOT an ancestor of `ugd-16/converge`, and
all 30 other branch tips ARE ancestors of converge -- verified mechanically with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor` over every ref. main's tree was missing 81 files,
including:

  * every `data/sources/*/SOURCE.lock.json` -- the reproducibility contract, 611
    files pinned by sha256. Without them a clone cannot verify that a
    re-acquisition produced the bytes the dictionary was built from;
  * the whole UGD-11d audit programme (`scripts/audit/*`: attribution coherence
    and precision probes, the verbatim-citation verifier and its mutation
    runners) that a user comment on the card explicitly required be shipped;
  * `src/bugd/{structure,reading,content}_corrections.py` and their data
    overlays -- the reviewable, byte-anchored source-defect corrections;
  * UGD-12's real-Yomitan behaviour/geometry suite and its harness;
  * `LICENSING.md`'s corrected audit and `scripts/_probe_ugd15_claims.py`.

The two files main had that converge does not are `src/bugd/corrections.py` and
its test -- the single correction module that converge deliberately split into
three (structure / reading / content), because they have different dataclasses,
data directories and pipeline stages. Nothing in this tree imports the old name.
They are dropped, not lost.

Three files main had that were worth keeping came over in an earlier commit on
this branch: the example-run-on fix, its evidence note, and
`scripts/check_example_runons.py`.

WHY THE RELEASE CHANGED

The release previously published for this repo (`v2026.09.09`) bundled ALL TEN
sources. Its own notes acknowledged shipping "a personal Anki deck, a paid
service (Bunpro), and published grammar content without an explicit
redistribution licence" from a public GitHub release. Verified by downloading the
asset: `tag_bank_1.json` declared all ten, `index.json` credited Bunpro and
DoJG 日本語文法辞典(全集), 4,632 entries.

That contradicts LICENSING.md, which finds eight of ten sources not publicly
redistributable. It has been deleted (release and tag; both URLs now 404).

The replacement is built through `bugd.publish_filter`: 1,550 entries from the
two sources whose CC BY 4.0 licence text is present in their own locked bytes
(NINJAL, Yokubi). `scripts/audit_public_archive.py` independently re-checks the
packaged bytes -- 0 hits for all eight excluded sources across EVERY member, both
admitted sources present and attributed in the tag bank and index attribution,
and the filter's admitted set equal to the set LICENSING.md pins.

VERIFIED ON THIS EXACT TREE

Replayed in a clean detached worktree with only ninjal_bunkei and yokubi acquired
-- precisely a public user's checkout. One `make public` produced
sha256 cc1d4aef01d9f5b20b1a6a97a3f3070e489b2f42b4d3689f6f49eeaf4fe6c06b
(483,953 B, 1,550 entries), byte-identical to the build in the development tree.
Pinned Yomitan schema validation and the independent Node/ajv validator both
accept it; audit-public FAILURES: none; 0 real example run-ons; the card contract
gate reports 0 invalid.

entry.title: UGD-17: skip a source whose LOCKED BYTES are unacquired, not whose di…
entry.content:
UGD-17: skip a source whose LOCKED BYTES are unacquired, not whose directory is missing

The skip in run_extract keyed on `data/sources/<name>/` existing. But
`SOURCE.lock.json` is committed for every source -- it IS the reproducibility
contract, 611 files pinned by sha256 -- so in a fresh clone every source
directory exists while holding only that lock. The check therefore skipped
NOTHING, and `make extract` died on the first unacquired source:

    SourceLockError: locked input is missing: data/sources/bunpou/文法.apkg

which made `make public` -- the one build a public user can actually run, since
by design they have only the two CC BY 4.0 sources -- unreachable. The
empty-corpus guard then fired correctly on 0 records, which is how this surfaced.

Keying on the locked PAYLOAD fixes it, and the skip is REPORTED with a reason
naming the missing members, because a silently smaller dictionary is precisely
the failure mode this project fails closed against. A malformed lock still
raises: that is a defect, not an unacquired source. An explicit `--source`
request still runs and still fails loudly.

Verified end to end in a clean detached worktree with ONLY ninjal_bunkei and
yokubi acquired -- exactly a public user's checkout: extract writes 932 points
and reports all 8 skips with reasons, and `make public` reproduces the published
archive BYTE-IDENTICALLY (cc1d4aef01d9f5b20b1a6a97a3f3070e489b2f42b4d3689f6f49eeaf4fe6c06b,
483,953 B, 1,550 entries), with audit-public FAILURES: none.

The full ten-source build is unchanged: 7,896 points, 0 skips.

Mutation: 3/3 killed -- reverting to the directory check, dropping the skip
report, and skipping everything each fail the assertion aimed at them.

entry.title: UGD-17: add the fail-closed publish gate LICENSING.md required, and s…
entry.content:
UGD-17: add the fail-closed publish gate LICENSING.md required, and ship the release

UGD-15's audit found eight of the ten acquired sources are not publicly
redistributable, and named the exact gap that blocked publication:

    "There is no publish-time filter. `redistributable` is recorded in
    provenance and carried through extraction, but no code in the build path
    reads it -- the flag appears only in the acquisition scripts that write it.
    It is therefore advisory metadata, not a machine-enforced gate."

This is that filter, plus the three real defects that surfaced building it.

THE GATE -- src/bugd/publish_filter.py + `make public`

`is_redistributable` requires TWO things, and the second one matters as much as
the first:

  * `provenance.redistributable is True` -- identity, not truthiness. `bunpro`
    and `imabi` carry no licence block in their SOURCE.lock at all, so a
    "not False" predicate would admit them on silence, and a `if flag:` test
    would admit the string "false".
  * `provenance.permissionBasis` is not a merely REPORTED permission. UGD-15
    separated "verified licence in locked bytes" (Yokubi, NINJAL) from
    "publishable only on reported permission, not independently verifiable"
    (IMABI: /terms/, /license/, /copyright/ all 404), and its instruction for
    the second class is to obtain the approval in writing first. So IMABI's 494
    lessons are excluded rather than shipped on an undocumented grant.

Filtering writes a SEPARATE `data/extracted-public/`, never editing the full
local corpus, and refuses to emit an empty public corpus -- a zero-entry archive
passes schema validation and would publish successfully while shipping nothing.
A source with a split grant raises instead of shipping the subset.

Every stage after the filter is the SAME code the local build runs, pointed at a
different directory, so the public artifact cannot drift from the one the tests
and audits cover.

THE INDEPENDENT CHECK -- scripts/audit_public_archive.py

The filter decides about INPUTS; this proves a fact about OUTPUTS. It scans every
member as text, because a leak need not be in a term bank: a `styles.css` comment
illustrating JLPT disagreement named two of the excluded community sources, so
the public archive shipped their names after the filter had removed all their
content. No content leaked, but an archive naming a source it deliberately
excluded is a false provenance claim; the comment is now source-agnostic.

The cleared set is PINNED from LICENSING.md, not derived from the filter's own
output. That distinction is the whole gate: an earlier version read the expected
set out of `data/extracted-public/`, so loosening the filter widened BOTH the
archive and the expectation and the audit reported "FAILURES: none" while IMABI
shipped. Verified by mutation -- that exact change survived until the pin existed.

THREE REAL DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY

  1. `yokubi.py` documented `redistributable: True` in its module docstring and
     never emitted the key. Every Yokubi record read `None`, so the publish
     filter excluded the one source whose CC BY 4.0 licence text is present in
     its own locked bytes. Invisible until something read the flag.

  2. `StaleCorrection` fired on any corpus narrower than the overlay. It is
     scoped now: a correction whose SOURCE contributes no rows is out of scope,
     not stale. A correction whose source IS present but whose row is gone still
     raises -- that is the drift the gate exists for. Both call sites (
     `reading_corrections.apply_corrections` and `unify`) were fixed; scoping one
     alone just moves the failure to the merge stage. This also resolves UGD-16's
     residual failure (c): the stage test now DECLARES its isolated corpus via a
     new `--no-reading-corrections` flag rather than the guard being weakened.

  3. `write_points_jsonl` wrote the reviewable sidecar BEFORE `ExtractResult`
     applied corrections and row identity, so bunpro's `points.jsonl` disagreed
     with the corpus the pipeline carried. Same stage-seam class as UGD-16's D1,
     and again only a round-trip equality assertion catches it, because the
     divergence is uniform and every count and digest still looks right.

PORTED: the example-sentence run-on fix

`banks.py`'s `_split_example_sentences` (from the abandoned `ugd-16/integration`
lineage, which is NOT an ancestor of this branch and is missing 81 files
including every SOURCE.lock, the UGD-11d audit automation, and UGD-12's suite).
Measured on this branch: REAL run-ons 144 -> 0 in the local archive, 27 -> 0 in
the public one. Committed with its evidence note and `check_example_runons.py`.

REPINS, attributed mechanically and never on a total

`test_corpus_counts_are_pinned` was stale by the four sources UGD-16 landed.
Attributed by rebuilding the keymap through the real production builder over the
same artifacts with those four `data/extracted/*.json` REMOVED:

  * that basis reports rows=5936 / substantiveRows=4696 exactly, reproducing the
    old pin, and the row-identity SETS differ by +1960 with ZERO lost
    (bunpou 534 + imabi 494 + ninjal_bunkei 800 + yokubi 132);
  * tierA 676->821 bijective, 201->217 refused, growing with the corpus;
  * tierB DECREASED 57->49, which a totals-only repin would have hidden. Set
    diff of `acceptedLinks`: +1 gained, 8 LOST. Verified nothing became
    unreachable -- all 16 forms are still separate points and 0 contributor
    identities disappeared -- so the pairs are split across two cards, not lost.
    Filed as its own card rather than fixed by loosening a fold guard here.

MUTATION EVIDENCE

  * publish_filter: 8/8 mutants killed, each by the assertion targeting it
    (absent-is-permitted, truthiness, no-provenance, reported-permission,
    empty-corpus, split grant, empty artifact, stale public dir).
  * Two mutants that SURVIVED were probe defects, not untested code: all 7,896
    records carry a boolean flag, so the missing-provenance and missing-key
    branches are unreachable through the corpus. They are covered by direct
    synthetic-input tests instead, which is the only thing that can kill them.
  * audit_public_archive: reintroducing an excluded producer's name fails it;
    dropping the reported-permission check fails it on TWO findings.
  * write_points_jsonl: dropping the normalization fails the bunpro round-trip.

VERIFIED

  Public:  1,550 entries (832 points + 718 redirects) from NINJAL + Yokubi only.
           sha256 identical across three consecutive builds. Pinned Yomitan
           schema validation and the independent Node/ajv validator both accept
           it. `audit-public` FAILURES: none -- 0 hits for all eight excluded
           sources across every member, both admitted sources present and
           attributed in tag bank and index. 0 real run-ons.
  Local:   4,901 entries, all ten sources, extract/keymap/merge/build/validate
           green, `audit-packaged` 26/26 FAILURES none.
  Suite:   662 passed. The 32 remaining failures are UGD-12's harness selectors
           against a stand-in that convergence replaced, reproduced on this
           branch's parent commit -- verified by running the same selection there.
  Clean:   126 tracked .py, every `bugd.*` import resolves to a tracked file,
           0 syntax errors.
